# Benchmarks

Measurements are reproducible guardrails and must not be presented as guarantees
from a single development machine. Run the checked-in headless profile with:

```bash
npm run benchmark
```

The `ci-safe-v1` profile lives in `packages/benchmarks`. It emits machine-readable
JSON and fails when a scenario exceeds the versioned ceiling in `baselines.json`.
CI runs it after a clean production build. Ceilings are intentionally broader
than a single workstation result so the gate detects major regressions without
encoding runner noise as product behavior.

## Initial baseline

Commit baseline environment: Windows x64, Node 24.12.0, warmup 1, samples 5.

| Scenario          | Fixture                                                 |                             Median |     p95 |     CI ceiling |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: |
| Composite         | 512 × 512, 12 full-canvas mixed-blend pixel layers      |                            2100 ms | 2148 ms | 4000 / 6000 ms |
| Brush             | 2048 × 2048 layer, 48 px pressure-aware diagonal stroke |                              43 ms |   50 ms |  500 / 1000 ms |
| Sparse tile patch | 32768 × 32768 transparent RGBA store, one 64 × 64 patch |                             2.3 ms |  3.8 ms |     25 / 75 ms |
| Sparse mask patch | 32768 × 32768 zero coverage store, one 64 × 64 patch    |                   recorded per run |       — |     25 / 75 ms |
| Document storage  | 1024 × 1024, 8 RGBA layers                              | 0.875× observed array-buffer delta |       — |          1.35× |
| Warm tile cache   | 128 × 128, 4 layers, dependency-keyed composite tiles   |                            ~0.5 ms | ~0.6 ms |    50 / 100 ms |

The memory fixture owns 33,554,432 logical pixel bytes. The first observed
array-buffer delta was 29,360,128 bytes (0.875×); garbage collection can make
the delta smaller than logical ownership, so only upward amplification is gated.
These numbers expose the current whole-surface compositor cost and provide the
comparison point for tiled storage and dirty-region rendering. The sparse tile
fixture allocates exactly one 256 × 256 tile (262,144 bytes) instead of a 4-GiB
contiguous surface; that allocation is also enforced by the baseline. The
one-channel mask fixture enforces a 65,536-byte tile ceiling rather than RGBA's
262,144 bytes.

The current checkpoint settles V8 memory accounting with three garbage
collection/event-loop turns before and after allocation. This keeps the
existing 1.35× guard unchanged while eliminating deferred backing-store noise.
The latest 33,554,432-byte fixture reports a 33,554,432-byte array-buffer delta
(1.00× amplification). This remains a Node guardrail, not browser peak-memory
evidence; browser working-set and long-task suites remain an M1/M2 priority.

Record, at minimum: commit, browser/version, OS, CPU, memory, device pixel
ratio, document dimensions, layer count, input encoding/size, warmup, sample
count, and median/p95. Candidate scenarios are cold application start, PNG/JPEG
decode, first render, repeated layer transform/composite, undo/redo, IndexedDB
save/restore, export, and repeated live Free Transform preview pointer moves.

Separate CPU time, wall time, peak memory, and output size. Use representative
documents that can be redistributed, keep the tab visible, and note throttling.
Correctness tests and memory/allocation limits take priority over benchmark
scores. Update a baseline only with an intentional architecture change, the raw
JSON report, and a documented fixture or environment revision.

`CompositeTileCache` proves warm dependency-keyed tiles assemble without re-invoking
the reference compositor. Latest Node result for 128 × 128 / 4 layers: warm median
~0.46 ms versus cold reference ~50 ms with `fullyWarm: true`. Cold full-frame
512 × 512 / 12-layer composite remains multi-second until the live path and
region-local population land.

# Benchmarks

Measurements are reproducible guardrails and must not be presented as guarantees
from a single development machine. Run the checked-in headless profile with:

```bash
npm run benchmark
```

The `ci-safe-v1` profile lives in `packages/benchmarks`. It emits machine-readable
JSON and fails when a scenario exceeds the versioned ceiling in `baselines.json`.
CI runs it after a clean production build. Ceilings are intentionally broader
than a single workstation result so the gate detects major regressions without
encoding runner noise as product behavior.

## Initial baseline

Commit baseline environment: Windows x64, Node 24.12.0, warmup 1, samples 5.

| Scenario          | Fixture                                                 |                             Median |     p95 |     CI ceiling |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: |
| Composite         | 512 × 512, 12 full-canvas mixed-blend pixel layers      |                            2100 ms | 2148 ms | 4000 / 6000 ms |
| Brush             | 2048 × 2048 layer, 48 px pressure-aware diagonal stroke |                              43 ms |   50 ms |  500 / 1000 ms |
| Sparse tile patch | 32768 × 32768 transparent RGBA store, one 64 × 64 patch |                             2.3 ms |  3.8 ms |     25 / 75 ms |
| Sparse mask patch | 32768 × 32768 zero coverage store, one 64 × 64 patch    |                   recorded per run |       — |     25 / 75 ms |
| Document storage  | 1024 × 1024, 8 RGBA layers                              | 0.875× observed array-buffer delta |       — |          1.35× |
| Warm tile cache   | 128 × 128, 4 layers, dependency-keyed composite tiles   |                            ~0.5 ms | ~0.6 ms |    50 / 100 ms |

The memory fixture owns 33,554,432 logical pixel bytes. The first observed
array-buffer delta was 29,360,128 bytes (0.875×); garbage collection can make
the delta smaller than logical ownership, so only upward amplification is gated.
These numbers expose the current whole-surface compositor cost and provide the
comparison point for tiled storage and dirty-region rendering. The sparse tile
fixture allocates exactly one 256 × 256 tile (262,144 bytes) instead of a 4-GiB
contiguous surface; that allocation is also enforced by the baseline. The
one-channel mask fixture enforces a 65,536-byte tile ceiling rather than RGBA's
262,144 bytes.

The current checkpoint settles V8 memory accounting with three garbage
collection/event-loop turns before and after allocation. This keeps the
existing 1.35× guard unchanged while eliminating deferred backing-store noise.
The latest 33,554,432-byte fixture reports a 33,554,432-byte array-buffer delta
(1.00× amplification). This remains a Node guardrail, not browser peak-memory
evidence; browser working-set and long-task suites remain an M1/M2 priority.

Record, at minimum: commit, browser/version, OS, CPU, memory, device pixel
ratio, document dimensions, layer count, input encoding/size, warmup, sample
count, and median/p95. Candidate scenarios are cold application start, PNG/JPEG
decode, first render, repeated layer transform/composite, undo/redo, IndexedDB
save/restore, export, and repeated live Free Transform preview pointer moves.

Separate CPU time, wall time, peak memory, and output size. Use representative
documents that can be redistributed, keep the tab visible, and note throttling.
Correctness tests and memory/allocation limits take priority over benchmark
scores. Update a baseline only with an intentional architecture change, the raw
JSON report, and a documented fixture or environment revision.

`CompositeTileCache` proves warm dependency-keyed tiles assemble without re-invoking
the reference compositor. Latest Node result for 128 × 128 / 4 layers: warm median
~0.46 ms versus cold reference ~50 ms with `fullyWarm: true`. Cold full-frame
512 × 512 / 12-layer composite remains multi-second until the live path and
region-local population land.

## Browser composite probe (M2 evidence)

`npm run test:browser-perf` runs Chromium Playwright against `window.__freetoshopPerf`.
Latest recorded probe (`docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-probe.json`):

| Metric                       |                                    Value |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------: |
| Fixture                      | 256 × 256, 8 mixed-blend layers, tile 64 |
| Cold median                  |                                  ~348 ms |

| Fully warm                   |                                     true |

Warm cache is more than 100× faster than cold reference recompose in the browser.
Node still records multi-second cold 512×512/12-layer full composites; the warm tile
path is the interactive path for repeated frames.

`CompositeWorkerScheduler`. While the worker is in flight, the UI uses

# Benchmarks

Measurements are reproducible guardrails and must not be presented as guarantees
from a single development machine. Run the checked-in headless profile with:

```bash
npm run benchmark
```

The `ci-safe-v1` profile lives in `packages/benchmarks`. It emits machine-readable
JSON and fails when a scenario exceeds the versioned ceiling in `baselines.json`.
CI runs it after a clean production build. Ceilings are intentionally broader
than a single workstation result so the gate detects major regressions without
encoding runner noise as product behavior.

## Initial baseline

Commit baseline environment: Windows x64, Node 24.12.0, warmup 1, samples 5.

| Scenario          | Fixture                                                 |                             Median |     p95 |     CI ceiling |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: |
| Composite         | 512 × 512, 12 full-canvas mixed-blend pixel layers      |                            2100 ms | 2148 ms | 4000 / 6000 ms |
| Brush             | 2048 × 2048 layer, 48 px pressure-aware diagonal stroke |                              43 ms |   50 ms |  500 / 1000 ms |
| Sparse tile patch | 32768 × 32768 transparent RGBA store, one 64 × 64 patch |                             2.3 ms |  3.8 ms |     25 / 75 ms |
| Sparse mask patch | 32768 × 32768 zero coverage store, one 64 × 64 patch    |                   recorded per run |       — |     25 / 75 ms |
| Document storage  | 1024 × 1024, 8 RGBA layers                              | 0.875× observed array-buffer delta |       — |          1.35× |
| Warm tile cache   | 128 × 128, 4 layers, dependency-keyed composite tiles   |                            ~0.5 ms | ~0.6 ms |    50 / 100 ms |

The memory fixture owns 33,554,432 logical pixel bytes. The first observed
array-buffer delta was 29,360,128 bytes (0.875×); garbage collection can make
the delta smaller than logical ownership, so only upward amplification is gated.
These numbers expose the current whole-surface compositor cost and provide the
comparison point for tiled storage and dirty-region rendering. The sparse tile
fixture allocates exactly one 256 × 256 tile (262,144 bytes) instead of a 4-GiB
contiguous surface; that allocation is also enforced by the baseline. The
one-channel mask fixture enforces a 65,536-byte tile ceiling rather than RGBA's
262,144 bytes.

The current checkpoint settles V8 memory accounting with three garbage
collection/event-loop turns before and after allocation. This keeps the
existing 1.35× guard unchanged while eliminating deferred backing-store noise.
The latest 33,554,432-byte fixture reports a 33,554,432-byte array-buffer delta
(1.00× amplification). This remains a Node guardrail, not browser peak-memory
evidence; browser working-set and long-task suites remain an M1/M2 priority.

Record, at minimum: commit, browser/version, OS, CPU, memory, device pixel
ratio, document dimensions, layer count, input encoding/size, warmup, sample
count, and median/p95. Candidate scenarios are cold application start, PNG/JPEG
decode, first render, repeated layer transform/composite, undo/redo, IndexedDB
save/restore, export, and repeated live Free Transform preview pointer moves.

Separate CPU time, wall time, peak memory, and output size. Use representative
documents that can be redistributed, keep the tab visible, and note throttling.
Correctness tests and memory/allocation limits take priority over benchmark
scores. Update a baseline only with an intentional architecture change, the raw
JSON report, and a documented fixture or environment revision.

## Composite tile cache (M2 foundation)

`CompositeTileCache` proves warm dependency-keyed tiles assemble without re-invoking
the reference compositor. Latest Node result for 128 × 128 / 4 layers: warm median
~0.46 ms versus cold reference ~50 ms with `fullyWarm: true`. Cold full-frame
512 × 512 / 12-layer composite remains multi-second until the live path and
region-local population land.

## Browser composite probe (M2 evidence)

`npm run test:browser-perf` runs Chromium Playwright against `window.__freetoshopPerf`.
Latest recorded probe (`docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-probe.json`):

| Metric                       |                                    Value |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------: |
| Fixture                      | 256 × 256, 8 mixed-blend layers, tile 64 |
| Cold median                  |                                  ~348 ms |
| Warm median                  |                                  ~0.8 ms |
| Visibility cold / warm       |                        ~282 ms / ~0.5 ms |
| Fully warm                   |                                     true |
| Long tasks during warm burst |                       0 ms (best-effort) |

Warm cache is more than 100× faster than cold reference recompose in the browser.
Node still records multi-second cold 512×512/12-layer full composites; the warm tile
path is the interactive path for repeated frames.

## Worker-scheduled composite (M2)

Cold advanced stacks may schedule a module worker (`kind: 'composite'`) via
`CompositeWorkerScheduler`. While the worker is in flight, the UI uses
`warmAssembleOnly` (no main-thread `referenceComposite` miss-fill). Matching
worker frames seed the tile cache. Browser evidence
(`docs/perf-evidence/browser-worker-composite-cold-path.json`, 128×128 / 6 layers):

| Metric                       |   Value |
| ---------------------------- | ------: |
| Main-thread reference        |  ~58 ms |
| Main-thread warmAssembleOnly |   ~1 ms |
| warmOnlyReferenceCalls       |       0 |
| Worker frame wait            | ~135 ms |
| workerMatchesReference       |    true |

Working-set probe (24 opacity edits, 128×128 / tile 64 / maxBytes 48 KiB):
`stayedWithinBudget: true`, `boundedGrowth: true`, `totalEvictions > 0`
(`docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-working-set.json`).

Larger cold path (256×256 / 8 layers): warmOnlyReferenceCalls=0, worker≡reference;
see `docs/perf-evidence/browser-worker-composite-cold-path-large.json`.

Long-session probe (120 opacity revisions, 192×192 / 8 layers / tile 64 /
maxBytes 96 KiB): `stayedWithinBudget: true`, `boundedGrowth: true`,
`peakAllocatedBytes == maxBytes`, `totalEvictions > 0`
(`docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-long-session.json`). Unit suite covers
an 80-edit multi-revision session under a tighter budget.

Large-document interactive probe (1024×1024 / 6 layers / tile 64 /
viewport 384×384, pan 512,256) after batched miss-union region fill:

| Metric                        |                                   Value |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------: |
| Cold progressive viewport     | **~64 ms** (was ~241 → ~526 → ~3608 ms) |
| Warm progressive viewport     |                                 ~2.9 ms |
| Pan cold (new region)         |         **~40 ms** (was ~226 → ~523 ms) |
| Pan warm                      |                                 ~2.1 ms |
| Return-home warm              |                                 ~1.9 ms |
| Mip-1 warm                    |                                 ~0.4 ms |
| Progressive first-paint tiles |                           36 / 256 full |
| Interactive budget (warm)     |                                   50 ms |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-large-doc-interactive.json` (re-probed after
region store-read + allocation-free surface blend + **normal/multiply/screen inline paths**).
Progressive cold viewport fill is now under 100 ms on this host for 1024²/6 layers.
Node progressive cold 512²/6 ~95 ms; unit 512² progressive cold budget <1s;
unit 4096² sparse progressive stays region-local (tileCount bounded, 0 full-ref misses).

Chromium suite: `npm run test:browser-perf` (includes live App pan/zoom E2E and
**4096² sparse progressive** writing `browser-composite-4k-sparse-interactive.json`:
cold ~34 ms / pan cold ~15 ms / warm ~5 ms, 36 of 4096 tiles).
**Tri-engine**: Firefox + WebKit pass large-doc progressive interactive probe
(`docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-large-doc-tri-engine.txt`). Dense 4k×20 and
8192 sparse progressive are tri-engine gated. Sustained progressive memory budgets
are recorded below (Chromium E2E).
Brush frame (Chromium): paint median ~0.8 ms, commit ~0.9 ms, frame ~1.7 ms on 2048² sparse
(`docs/perf-evidence/browser-brush-frame-interactive.json`).

### Dense large-document progressive (M2)

| Probe                                   | Result                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Unit 2048²/4 dense progressive viewport | ~0.6 s (budget <5 s), region-local, 0 full-ref |
| Unit 4096²/2 dense progressive viewport | ~0.7 s (budget <8 s), region-local, 0 full-ref |
| Browser 2048²/4 dense progressive cold  | **~53 ms**                                        |
| Browser 2048² pan cold                  | **~31 ms**                                        |
| Browser 2048² warm                      | **~4 ms**                                         |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-2048-dense-interactive.json`.

| Browser 4096²/2 dense progressive cold | **~47 ms** |
| Browser 4096²/2 pan cold | **~28 ms** |
| Browser 4096²/2 warm | **~9 ms** |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-4096-dense-interactive.json`.

| Browser 4096²/6 dense progressive cold | **~96 ms** |
| Browser 4096²/6 pan cold | **~64 ms** |
| Browser 4096²/6 warm | **~20 ms** |
| Unit 4096²/6 dense progressive home+pan | ~3.9 s (budget 15 s), budget-bounded bytes |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-4096-dense-x6-interactive.json`.

| Unit 4096²/12 dense progressive home+pan | ~4.3 s (budget 30 s), region-local |

### Representative 4096×4096 × 20 layers (M2 goal fixture)

| Probe                     | Result                                                                |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Unit progressive home+pan | ~7.7 s construction+compose, region-local, warm reassemble <500 ms |
| Browser progressive cold  | **~232 ms**                                                           |
| Browser pan cold          | **~198 ms**                                                           |
| Browser warm              | **~45 ms** (<50 ms interactive budget)                             |
| Progressive tiles         | 36 / 4096 full                                                        |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-4096-dense-x20-interactive.json`.

### 8192×8192 sparse document (M2 goal fixture)

| Probe                     | Result                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Unit progressive home+pan | region-local, <10 s budget (~84 ms host) |
| Browser progressive cold  | **~39 ms**                                  |
| Browser pan cold          | **~20 ms**                                  |
| Browser warm              | **~10 ms**                                  |
| Progressive tiles         | 36 / 16384 full                             |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-8192-sparse-interactive.json`.

### Sustained progressive pan memory (M2)

| Probe                                      | Result                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Fixture                                    | 1024² / 6 layers / tile 64 / viewport 384 / 48 pan+edit iterations |
| Cache budget                               | **2.5 MiB** (≪ 24 MiB full multi-layer surface)                    |
| Peak allocated                             | **2.5 MiB** (at budget)                                            |
| Final allocated                            | **2.5 MiB**                                                        |
| Total LRU evictions                        | **1024**                                                           |
| Peak unique spatial tiles                  | **158 / 256** full grid (~0.62)                                    |
| Peak entry count                           | **160** (dependency-key revisions can exceed unique spatial)       |
| Stayed within budget                       | **true**                                                           |
| Bounded growth (2nd half ≤ 1.25× 1st half) | **true**                                                           |
| Progressive sparse vs full multi-layer     | **true** (peak < fullMultiLayerBytes)                           |

Evidence: `docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-large-doc-sustained-memory.json`
(Chromium E2E `large document progressive pan session keeps tile memory bounded`).
**Tri-engine**: Firefox + WebKit also pass the same sustained-memory gate (peak at
budget, evictions > 0, unique spatial < full grid, progressiveSparseVsFull).
`CompositeTileCache.stats.uniqueSpatialTileCount` separates spatial footprint from
dependency-key entry churn so revision history does not look like unbounded spatial growth.

# FreetoShop Implementation Roadmap

## Contract and status rules

This roadmap tracks the complete near-Photopea build contract. It does not
reduce the intended scope, and a polished UI or passing smoke test is not
evidence of parity. The current repository and its executable tests are the
implementation authority.

Every subsystem has exactly one maturity level:

- **Not started:** no production implementation.
- **Foundation only:** interfaces or a narrow first path exist, but ordinary
  product workflows do not depend on them comprehensively.
- **Partially integrated:** a real user workflow uses the subsystem, with
  documented feature, performance, or compatibility gaps.
- **Functionally complete:** the required behavior exists across ordinary
  workflows, but parity, stress, compatibility, or release hardening remains.
- **Compatibility-hardened:** broad corpora, cross-engine behavior, malformed
  inputs, migrations, and regression suites pass; operational release work may
  remain.
- **Production-ready:** the original definition of done is met, including
  performance, security, accessibility, documentation, and release evidence.

No subsystem is currently production-ready. Status changes require concrete
implementation, tests, benchmark or runtime evidence where relevant, and a
record of remaining limitations.

## Active critical path

1. Make tiled resources canonical for pixel layers, masks, editing, history,
   persistence, PSD decode, and export boundaries.
2. Connect exact edit bounds to a real tile render scheduler with dependency
   caching, progressive viewport work, mip levels, eviction, and cancellation.
3. Establish reproducible tri-engine browser performance and memory suites.
4. Continue incremental `App.tsx` decomposition as each workflow is touched.
5. Expand PSD support through preservation-first parsing before any PSD export.
6. Evolve the native container only after canonical tile ownership stabilizes.
7. Continue the remaining professional editor, compatibility, and production
   hardening contract without substituting shallow toolbar breadth for the
   critical path above.

## Imminent professional-editing queue

These are the next user-prioritized compatibility slices after the active M1/M2
infrastructure gate. Their order is intentional; a slice is complete only when
its editing workflow, history behavior, persistence, focused tests, and
tri-engine runtime path pass together.

1. **Clone Stamp:** sampled-source tiled strokes with aligned/unaligned modes,
   transformed-layer coordinates, selection/mask clipping, undo, and reopen.
2. **Healing Brush foundation:** sampled texture transfer with deterministic
   tone/color blending, bounded tile reads, selection clipping, undo, and
   reopen.
3. **Curves:** editable RGB composite curve with stable interpolation, live
   preview, adjustment-layer persistence, destructive application, and undo.
4. **Layer alignment/distribution/linking:** multi-layer targeting, canvas or
   selection reference bounds, deterministic alignment/distribution, persisted
   links, linked movement, and atomic undo.
5. **Perspective/distort:** four-corner transform preview/apply for layers and
   masks, bounded resampling, cancel, undo, and reopen.
6. **Brush dynamics and pressure:** pointer-pressure size/opacity mapping,
   deterministic mouse fallback, persisted controls/presets, and replayable
   stroke history.
7. **Select and Mask:** edge-refinement controls and preview modes that can
   output a selection or raster mask while preserving sparse coverage.
8. **Better text controls:** character/paragraph controls for ranges, font
   selection, size, leading, tracking, alignment, and persisted editable text.

# FreetoShop Implementation Roadmap

## Contract and status rules

This roadmap tracks the complete near-Photopea build contract. It does not
reduce the intended scope, and a polished UI or passing smoke test is not
evidence of parity. The current repository and its executable tests are the
implementation authority.

Every subsystem has exactly one maturity level:

- **Not started:** no production implementation.
- **Foundation only:** interfaces or a narrow first path exist, but ordinary
  product workflows do not depend on them comprehensively.
- **Partially integrated:** a real user workflow uses the subsystem, with
  documented feature, performance, or compatibility gaps.
- **Functionally complete:** the required behavior exists across ordinary
  workflows, but parity, stress, compatibility, or release hardening remains.
- **Compatibility-hardened:** broad corpora, cross-engine behavior, malformed
  inputs, migrations, and regression suites pass; operational release work may
  remain.
- **Production-ready:** the original definition of done is met, including
  performance, security, accessibility, documentation, and release evidence.

No subsystem is currently production-ready. Status changes require concrete
implementation, tests, benchmark or runtime evidence where relevant, and a
record of remaining limitations.

## Active critical path

1. Make tiled resources canonical for pixel layers, masks, editing, history,
   persistence, PSD decode, and export boundaries.
2. Connect exact edit bounds to a real tile render scheduler with dependency
   caching, progressive viewport work, mip levels, eviction, and cancellation.
3. Establish reproducible tri-engine browser performance and memory suites.
4. Continue incremental `App.tsx` decomposition as each workflow is touched.
5. Expand PSD support through preservation-first parsing before any PSD export.
6. Evolve the native container only after canonical tile ownership stabilizes.
7. Continue the remaining professional editor, compatibility, and production
   hardening contract without substituting shallow toolbar breadth for the
   critical path above.

## Imminent professional-editing queue

These are the next user-prioritized compatibility slices after the active M1/M2
infrastructure gate. Their order is intentional; a slice is complete only when
its editing workflow, history behavior, persistence, focused tests, and
tri-engine runtime path pass together.

1. **Clone Stamp:** sampled-source tiled strokes with aligned/unaligned modes,
   transformed-layer coordinates, selection/mask clipping, undo, and reopen.
2. **Healing Brush foundation:** sampled texture transfer with deterministic
   tone/color blending, bounded tile reads, selection clipping, undo, and
   reopen.
3. **Curves:** editable RGB composite curve with stable interpolation, live
   preview, adjustment-layer persistence, destructive application, and undo.
4. **Layer alignment/distribution/linking:** multi-layer targeting, canvas or
   selection reference bounds, deterministic alignment/distribution, persisted
   links, linked movement, and atomic undo.
5. **Perspective/distort:** four-corner transform preview/apply for layers and
   masks, bounded resampling, cancel, undo, and reopen.
6. **Brush dynamics and pressure:** pointer-pressure size/opacity mapping,
   deterministic mouse fallback, persisted controls/presets, and replayable
   stroke history.
7. **Select and Mask:** edge-refinement controls and preview modes that can
   output a selection or raster mask while preserving sparse coverage.
8. **Better text controls:** character/paragraph controls for ranges, font
   selection, size, leading, tracking, alignment, and persisted editable text.

# FreetoShop

FreetoShop is a local-first, browser-based image editor. Its working foundation
now includes the first Phase B raster workflow. It is not yet a claim of
feature parity with Photoshop or any other commercial editor.

## Current scope

Phase A provides a strict TypeScript monorepo, a headless document/command
model, affine layer rendering through Canvas 2D, undo/redo, PNG/JPEG
import and export, content-addressed incremental IndexedDB persistence, a PWA shell, and responsive accessible
UI. Phase B adds a pressure-aware hard/soft round brush, eraser, rectangular
full-resolution selections with replace/add/subtract/intersect algebra,
selection-constrained brightness, layer movement, and nondestructive pixel-layer
raster masks with enable, density, inversion, persistence, and direct
selection-aware Brush/Eraser editing. Shape, text, and smart-object layers expose
the same local raster-mask controls and painting without rasterizing their source.
Groups expose the same controls through canvas-sized document-space raster masks
that constrain the combined pass-through or isolated result.
Pixels and masks are explicit edit targets,
and each pointer gesture is a single undoable transaction. Saved full-resolution
alpha channels can be created from selections, renamed, previewed, restored as a
selection, deleted, undone/redone, and recovered locally. Composite RGB channels
also have read-only grayscale inspection views, while export always uses the
unchanged composite document. Layers, Channels, and History are functional,
keyboard-navigable panels. Layers now use canonical affine matrices with nested
group composition, numeric matrix/position editing, centered 90-degree rotation,
horizontal/vertical flipping, reset, transformed painting and adjustment
coordinates, undo/redo, export, and local recovery. Free Transform adds
constant-screen-size accessible corner/edge scale and rotation handles, body
translation, live nondestructive preview, Shift-constrained scaling, keyboard
handle operation, Escape cancellation, and one history transaction per pointer
gesture. The Crop tool accepts a canvas drag or exact integer bounds, previews
the proposed rectangle, and commits one undoable canvas change. Cropping keeps
layer-local pixels and raster masks intact, translates root-layer placement,
remaps selections and saved alpha channels, and is preserved by local recovery
and PNG export. Crop, Canvas Size, Reveal All, and Image Size limit canvases to
32,768 pixels per axis and 100,000,000 pixels in total. Canvas Size can grow or
trim around any of nine anchors while preserving layer resources and remapping
selections and saved
channels. Reveal All expands, but never shrinks, the canvas to contain the
transformed bounds of visible, nonzero-opacity pixel layers. Image Size
resamples raster layers, masks, selections, and channels with nearest-neighbor
or bilinear pixel-center sampling; RGBA bilinear interpolation uses
premultiplied alpha. It preserves nested affine placement. All three operations
are undoable and survive PNG export and local recovery. Phase B selection tools
now include a four-times-supersampled ellipse, a freehand lasso converted to an
antialiased even-odd polygon, and a composite-image Magic Wand with 0–255
tolerance and contiguous/global matching. All selection tools support replace,
add, subtract, and intersect; full-resolution masks can be feathered, expanded,
contracted, smoothed, bordered, saved as alpha channels, undone, and recovered.
File → Export Selection PNG composites only the selected bounds and applies soft
selection coverage to the exported alpha channel.
Canvas chrome follows the actual arbitrary mask boundary instead of reducing it
to a bounding rectangle. The Wand samples the flattened composite, includes
alpha, and uses four-neighbor connectivity in Contiguous mode.

The destructive Filters dialog provides live, cancellable previews and one-step
application of Contrast, Levels, Hue/Saturation, Invert, Grayscale, Threshold,
Posterize, and Gaussian Blur. Filters respect soft document selections through
nested affine layer placement while changing only the selected pixel layer's
source pixels. Gaussian Blur is separable, edge-clamped, and
premultiplied-alpha aware, with an integer radius from 0 through 100.

The schema-v12 layer stack supports 26 deterministic professional blend modes:
the Darken/Lighten families, Dodge/Burn families, contrast families, Difference,
Exclusion, Subtract, Divide, and the nonseparable Hue, Saturation, Color, and
Luminosity modes in addition to Normal. Advanced stacks use a deterministic
premultiplied-alpha CPU compositor;
ordinary Normal-only stacks retain the direct Canvas path. Layers have separate
opacity and fill opacity, clipping relationships, transparency/pixel/position/all
locks, and visible state badges. Isolated groups composite into an intermediate
surface, while pass-through groups feed their children into the parent stack.
Editable Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Hue/Saturation, and Invert adjustment
layers render nondestructively, can be clipped, and support enableable,
density-adjustable document-space raster masks. These properties, payloads, and
masks round-trip through IndexedDB. Schema v7 also stores editable shape layers
plus multiline text layers with font family, size, weight, italic, line height,
alignment, and color. Rectangle, ellipse, and arbitrary line/cubic vector paths
retain editable fill, stroke, dimensions, commands, anchors, control points, and
corner radius where applicable. The Pen tool creates open or closed paths;
selected paths expose transformed on-canvas anchors and Bézier controls with
pointer dragging, keyboard nudging, live preview, cancellation, and one-step undo;
structured layers participate in transforms,
blending, clipping, grouping, duplication, recovery, compositing, and PNG export.
Local TrueType/OpenType font loading activates lazy HarfBuzz shaping with
kerning, standard/contextual ligatures, inferred LTR/RTL direction, positioned
glyph outlines, and shaped line wrapping. The text panel identifies when a
layer is using that professional path. System fonts remain an explicit Canvas
fallback when their binary data is unavailable.
Pixel, shape, and text layers share accessible Free Transform handles and
keyboard rotation/scaling without rasterizing structured content.
Editable color overlay, outside stroke, and drop-shadow layer effects share the
same nondestructive display/export compositor and remain adjustable after local
recovery. Renderable layers can be converted into embedded smart objects without
flattening their source. Smart objects retain an owned nested layer tree,
composite recursively, transform nondestructively, accept effects, support local
raster replacement, and open in an isolated full editor session. Saving source
edits creates one parent undo step; cancelling restores the untouched parent.
They survive export and recovery. Each smart object also owns an ordered,
enableable smart-filter stack with editable opacity. Invert, Grayscale, Gaussian
Blur, and Brightness/Contrast render nondestructively between the nested source
composite and the object's outer mask/effects. Nesting is capped at 16 levels.
Pixel, shape, text, smart-object, adjustment, and group layers support an independent editable vector mask with owned path
commands, enable/disable, density, inversion, undo/redo, export, and recovery.
Vector and raster masks multiply nondestructively when both are present.
Schemas v1-v15 migrate explicitly. Group masks apply in document space to the combined
pass-through or isolated group result.
The layer panel also supports Ctrl/Command multiselect, recursive duplication,
grouping of common-parent layers, visual hierarchy indentation, safe ungrouping
of Normal pass-through groups, multi-delete, root-layer merging, and flattening
visible content. Structural operations are single history transactions and
survive local recovery. Merge and Flatten rasterize through the same compositor
used by PNG export, so nondestructive adjustments are baked only when the user
explicitly chooses one of those commands.

Initial import-only PSD support recognizes the binary signature, validates
8-bit RGB PSD v1 files, and parses them in a cancellable worker. Pixel layers,
placement, supported blend modes, visibility, opacity, locks, clipping, and
nested groups translate into editable native layers. Structured previews are
rasterized and unsupported content is reported; masks, effects, channels,
metadata, PSB, higher bit depths, non-RGB modes, and PSD saving remain
unsupported. Keep the original PSD because FreetoShop does not preserve it for
round-trip export.

Save document or Ctrl/Command+S downloads the editable `.freetoshop` native
format. Version 2 stores canonical schema metadata plus binary pixel and coverage
tiles once per SHA-256 content ID; the outer payload and every resource are
validated before a worker replaces the current document. Legacy v1 JSON files
still open. The downloaded file remains a complete snapshot rather than an
incrementally updated or compressed large-document format.

Mixed-direction bidi paragraphs, vertical text, text-on-path, per-character
styles, variable-font controls, font fallback, and font embedding remain
unsupported. Boolean path operations,
linked/reusable smart
object instances, editable/spot channels, perspective and
warp transforms, smart-filter masks/blend options and broader professional filter
families, advanced color workflows, plugins, scripting, and PSD/PSB round-trip
interoperability remain unsupported. Image resizing currently operates on 8-bit
sRGB-like buffers in memory; bilinear is not an area-reduction filter, and tiled
or high-bit-depth image backends are not implemented. Selection algorithms and
live filter previews remain synchronous; committed filters and image resampling
run in module workers. The editor does not yet provide
magnetic/quick or object-aware selection, color range, refine-edge analysis, GPU
processing, or a broader nondestructive filter library. The current advanced
compositor is whole-canvas and CPU-bound. A sparse tiled storage and dirty-region
rendering foundation exists, but canonical layer storage has not migrated to it
and rendering is not GPU-accelerated;
pass-through group opacity is applied to children and does not yet implement
every Photoshop knockout/effect interaction.

The project is private and under active development. Expect file formats and
internal APIs to change before a compatibility promise is published.

npm install
npm run dev
```

npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run audit
npm run build

publishes `apps/web/dist`, and uses the same Node/npm versions as local and CI
validation. The browser CI job builds that production output before launching
the preview server.

# Benchmarks

Measurements are reproducible guardrails and must not be presented as guarantees
from a single development machine. Run the checked-in headless profile with:

```bash
npm run benchmark
```

The `ci-safe-v1` profile lives in `packages/benchmarks`. It emits machine-readable
JSON and fails when a scenario exceeds the versioned ceiling in `baselines.json`.
CI runs it after a clean production build. Ceilings are intentionally broader
than a single workstation result so the gate detects major regressions without
encoding runner noise as product behavior.

## Initial baseline

Commit baseline environment: Windows x64, Node 24.12.0, warmup 1, samples 5.

| Scenario          | Fixture                                                 |                             Median |     p95 |     CI ceiling |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: |
| Composite         | 512 × 512, 12 full-canvas mixed-blend pixel layers      |                            2100 ms | 2148 ms | 4000 / 6000 ms |
| Brush             | 2048 × 2048 layer, 48 px pressure-aware diagonal stroke |                              43 ms |   50 ms |  500 / 1000 ms |
| Sparse tile patch | 32768 × 32768 transparent RGBA store, one 64 × 64 patch |                             2.3 ms |  3.8 ms |     25 / 75 ms |
| Sparse mask patch | 32768 × 32768 zero coverage store, one 64 × 64 patch    |                   recorded per run |       — |     25 / 75 ms |
| Document storage  | 1024 × 1024, 8 RGBA layers                              | 0.875× observed array-buffer delta |       — |          1.35× |
| Warm tile cache   | 128 × 128, 4 layers, dependency-keyed composite tiles   |                            ~0.5 ms | ~0.6 ms |    50 / 100 ms |

The memory fixture owns 33,554,432 logical pixel bytes. The first observed
array-buffer delta was 29,360,128 bytes (0.875×); garbage collection can make
the delta smaller than logical ownership, so only upward amplification is gated.
These numbers expose the current whole-surface compositor cost and provide the
comparison point for tiled storage and dirty-region rendering. The sparse tile
fixture allocates exactly one 256 × 256 tile (262,144 bytes) instead of a 4-GiB
contiguous surface; that allocation is also enforced by the baseline. The
one-channel mask fixture enforces a 65,536-byte tile ceiling rather than RGBA's
262,144 bytes.

The current checkpoint settles V8 memory accounting with three garbage
collection/event-loop turns before and after allocation. This keeps the
existing 1.35× guard unchanged while eliminating deferred backing-store noise.
The latest 33,554,432-byte fixture reports a 33,554,432-byte array-buffer delta
(1.00× amplification). This remains a Node guardrail, not browser peak-memory
evidence; browser working-set and long-task suites remain an M1/M2 priority.

Record, at minimum: commit, browser/version, OS, CPU, memory, device pixel
ratio, document dimensions, layer count, input encoding/size, warmup, sample
count, and median/p95. Candidate scenarios are cold application start, PNG/JPEG
decode, first render, repeated layer transform/composite, undo/redo, IndexedDB
save/restore, export, and repeated live Free Transform preview pointer moves.

Separate CPU time, wall time, peak memory, and output size. Use representative
documents that can be redistributed, keep the tab visible, and note throttling.
Correctness tests and memory/allocation limits take priority over benchmark
scores. Update a baseline only with an intentional architecture change, the raw
JSON report, and a documented fixture or environment revision.

## Composite tile cache (M2 foundation)

`CompositeTileCache` proves warm dependency-keyed tiles assemble without re-invoking
the reference compositor. Latest Node result for 128 × 128 / 4 layers: warm median
~0.46 ms versus cold reference ~50 ms with `fullyWarm: true`. Cold full-frame
512 × 512 / 12-layer composite remains multi-second until the live path and
region-local population land.

## Browser composite probe (M2 evidence)

`npm run test:browser-perf` runs Chromium Playwright against `window.__freetoshopPerf`.
Latest recorded probe (`docs/perf-evidence/browser-composite-probe.json`):

| Metric                       |                                    Value |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------: |
| Fixture                      | 256 × 256, 8 mixed-blend layers, tile 64 |
| Cold median                  |                                  ~348 ms |
| Warm median                  |                                  ~0.8 ms |
| Visibility cold / warm       |                        ~282 ms / ~0.5 ms |
| Fully warm                   |                                     true |
| Long tasks during warm burst |                       0 ms (best-effort) |

Warm cache is more than 100× faster than cold reference recompose in the browser.
Node still records multi-second cold 512×512/12-layer full composites; the warm tile
path is the interactive path for repeated frames.

## Worker-scheduled composite (M2)

Cold advanced stacks may schedule a module worker (`kind: 'composite'`) via
`CompositeWorkerScheduler`. While the worker is in flight, the UI uses
`warmAssembleOnly` (no main-thread `referenceComposite` miss-fill). Matching
worker frames seed the tile cache. Browser evidence
